q: Apart from watching over the building's physical state, what added task does Sec. 2.1.1(c) place on the Architect under Building Maintenance?
o: Conducting yearly structural audits under a separate SPP document
Issuing occupancy permits
Personally handling tenant lease negotiations
Monitoring security services
n: Sec. 2.1.1(c) simply states the Architect shall "monitor security services." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.1(c))

q: When an architect is kept on post-turnover as Building Administrator and/or Property Manager of a commercial complex, Sec. 1.3 says this role serves what underlying purpose?
o: To shield the architect from liability for any design errors
To extend the building's useful life so as to yield the greatest economic return
To satisfy a rule requiring only architects to manage buildings
To ready the building for eventual demolition
n: Sec. 1.3 states the Architect may be engaged as Building Administrator and/or Property Manager "to maximize the lifespan of the building/s in order to produce the maximum economic return." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.3)

q: Which areas' cleanliness must the Architect monitor under the maintenance and upkeep services described in Sec. 2.1.1(d)?
o: Solely the tenant units themselves
Solely the perimeter fence and guardhouse
Corridors, lobbies, stairways, other common areas, exits, parking areas, and garbage collection
Solely the main lobby and building signage
n: Sec. 2.1.1(d) covers "cleanliness of corridors, lobbies, stairs and other common areas, exits, parking areas, garbage collection." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.1(d))

q: When a building owner suspects the facility no longer serves its original purpose, which Sec. 2.2.1(a) evaluation task speaks directly to that concern?
o: Filing a fresh building permit application
Recomputing the architect's original design fee
Weighing the initial design program against the facility's actual use
Re-surveying the property's lot boundaries
n: Sec. 2.2.1(a) requires the Architect to "evaluate the initial design program vs. the actual use of the facility." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(a))

q: For Building Equipment Maintenance under Sec. 2.1.3, which equipment does the Architect help ensure stays properly maintained and functional?
o: Solely the architect's own drafting instruments
Air-conditioning units, the sprinkler system, generators, transformers, and telecommunications equipment
Solely elevators and escalators
Solely office furniture and fixtures
n: Sec. 2.1.3(a) lists "air-conditioning, sprinkler system, generators, transformers, telecommunications equipment, etc." as equipment the Architect helps ensure is properly maintained. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.3(a))

q: Which statute's IRR does SPP Document 205 form a part of?
o: Presidential Decree No. 1096 (the National Building Code)
Republic Act No. 9266 (the Architecture Act of 2004)
Republic Act No. 8981
Republic Act No. 545
n: The document's title block states it is "Part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266," the Architecture Act of 2004. (Source: SPP Document 205, title block)

q: When the same architect who designed and built a commercial complex is later tapped to also run its post-construction services, with no separate consultant brought in, which Sec. 3 arrangement does this fit?
o: Requiring a distinct license as Property Manager before proceeding
A setup barred outright under SPP Document 205
Serving solely as Consulting Architect for post-construction services (Sec. 3.2)
A dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect for post-construction services (Sec. 3.1)
n: Sec. 3.1 describes exactly this dual-capacity arrangement, where the same architect who was Architect-of-record also serves as Consulting Architect for post-construction services. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 3.1)

q: When Sec. 2.2.1(d) mentions "forensic investigation," it points the reader toward which other SPP document?
o: SPP Document 204
SPP Document 201
SPP Document 203
SPP Document 206
n: The text states "This is referred to as 'forensic investigation' of the building's systems (Reference Doc 203)." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(d))

q: Sec. 2.1.2 (Grounds and Landscaping Supervision) has the Architect overseeing landscape contractors and gardeners toward which specific end?
o: Structurally retrofitting retaining walls
Sourcing plant-nursery suppliers exclusively
Ensuring proper watering, pruning, trimming, and general upkeep of both hardscapes and softscapes
Installing new landscape lighting fixtures
n: Sec. 2.1.2(a) states the Architect shall "supervise landscape contractors and gardeners for the proper watering, pruning, trimming and maintenance of the landscape (both hardscapes and softscapes)." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.2(a))

q: During Post-Construction Evaluation, Sec. 2.2.1(b) has the Architect gauge how effective which elements are?
o: The building's insurance coverage alone
The land's tax assessment alone
The various building systems and the materials systems in use
The marketing strategy used to sell building units
n: Sec. 2.2.1(b) states the Architect shall "determine the effectiveness of the various building systems and the materials systems in use." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(b))

q: Years after turnover, shrinkage cracks and water seepage turn up in a building. What does Sec. 2.2.1(d) task the Architect to do about this, and what term is used for that activity?
o: Refer the matter solely to the local building official, with no further architect role
Rebuild the affected section immediately, at the architect's own cost
Look into the defects and propose solutions — an activity termed "forensic investigation" of the building's systems
Disregard it, since such post-construction defects fall outside SPP Document 205's coverage
n: Sec. 2.2.1(d) requires the Architect to study, research and give solutions to discovered/emerging/evolving defects and failures such as shrinkage and water seepage, and the document calls this a "forensic investigation" of the building's systems. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(d))

q: Sec. 2.1.4 (Business Development and Management) covers which pair of duties, matching an architect who wants to raise occupancy and correctly bill tenants for shared costs?
o: Drafting the building's original architectural design and obtaining the building permit
Negotiating the building's sale on the owner's behalf
Setting the assessed value of the property for real-property tax purposes
Devising schemes to maximize occupancy, and billing tenants for rent and utilities such as electricity, water, telephone, cable, and gas
n: Sec. 2.1.4 assigns the Architect to innovate schemes for maximum occupancy (2.1.4a) and to bill tenants for rentals and utilities such as electricity, water, telephone, cable, gas and other related dues (2.1.4b). (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.4(a)-(b))

q: Sec. 1.1 says building administration and management exceeds plain maintenance and upkeep because it calls for what type of professional?
o: A single-discipline maintenance contractor
A government building inspector
A civil engineer licensed solely for structural upkeep
A multi-disciplinary professional capable of a wide range of functions for efficient, economical building operation
n: Sec. 1.1 states building administration and management requires "the services of a multi-disciplinary professional who can perform a wide range or functions for the efficient and economical operation and maintenance of a building, facility or a complex." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.1)

q: Sec. 3 (Manner of Providing Services) recognizes two ways the Architect may contract with the Owner. Which pair is correct?
o: Exclusively through government appointment, or exclusively through private bidding
Only as a salaried employee of the Owner, or only as an unpaid volunteer consultant
A dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect for post-construction services, or solely as Consulting Architect for post-construction services
Only during the construction period, or only once the defects-liability period has ended
n: Sec. 3.1 and 3.2 give exactly these two manners of engagement. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 3.1-3.2)

q: Beyond landscape supervision, what else must the Architect keep up per Sec. 2.1.2(b) and (c)?
o: Solely the swimming pool and clubhouse facilities
Public roads beyond the property line, under LGU jurisdiction
Solely the building's exterior paint finish
Orderly entrances, exits, and parking areas, along with streets (road rights-of-way), walkways, and ramps
n: Sec. 2.1.2(b) covers maintaining orderly entrances, exits and parking areas; Sec. 2.1.2(c) covers maintaining streets, i.e., road rights-of-way (RROWs), walkways, and ramps. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.2(b)-(c))

q: Sec. 4 (Method of Compensation) allows the Architect to be paid for post-construction services in what manner?
o: Reimbursable expenses alone, with no professional fee permitted
A percentage of the total construction cost only, per SPP Document 202
A one-time fixed lump sum, payable before construction even starts
A percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees, and/or a monthly salary or fee
n: Sec. 4.1 allows a percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees, and/or (Sec. 4.2) a monthly salary/fee. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 4.1-4.2)

q: Sec. 1.2 says keeping communication open among owners, operators, architects, engineers, builders, and other parties serves what informational purpose for Post-Construction Services?
o: Access to information on the building's performance and upkeep
Access to information on the lot's zoning classification
Access to information on the owner's insurance premiums
Access to information on the original design fees paid to the architect
n: Sec. 1.2 says the open channels of communication exist "to provide access to information regarding the performance and upkeep of buildings." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.2)

q: SPP Document 205 covers what subject matter, and which earlier issuance did it replace?
o: The Code of Ethics for Architects, replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 205
The Standard of Professional Practice on Pre-Design Services, replacing UAP Doc. 201
The Standard of Professional Practice on Construction Supervision, an entirely new document with no predecessor
The Standard of Professional Practice on Post-Construction Services, replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 205
n: SPP Document 205 is titled "Post-Construction Services" and expressly states it is replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 205. (Source: SPP Document 205, title block)

q: Among the Architect's Building Maintenance duties is formulating and enforcing rules for the building's proper use — which areas does the source single out for emphasis?
o: Solely the owner's private office spaces
Solely the rooftop and basement levels
Common areas and the emergency, egress, and exit areas
Solely areas leased to third-party tenants
n: Sec. 2.1.1(b) directs the Architect to formulate and enforce rules for proper use of the building, "particularly in the common areas and the emergency/egress/exit areas." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.1(b))

q: What condition triggers the Architect's undertaking of Post-Construction Evaluation under Sec. 2.2?
o: It happens automatically each calendar year, whether or not the Owner wants it
It occurs only after a total building collapse
It is undertaken upon the Owner's request
It occurs only on order of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture
n: Sec. 2.2.1 begins: "Upon the request of the Owner, the Architect shall..." — evaluation is Owner-initiated, not automatic. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1)

q: Sec. 2.1.1 (Building Maintenance) has the Architect ensure the building and its parts are kept in good condition. Which set of parts does the source name?
o: Foundation, fire exits, and elevators only
Roofing, elevators, generators, and security cameras only
Structure, plumbing, electrical systems, partitions, and finishes
Structure, landscaping, signage, and parking
n: Sec. 2.1.1(a) requires the Architect to see that "the building and all the parts thereof (structure, plumbing, electrical, partitions, finishes, etc.) are all in good condition." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.1.1(a))

q: Sec. 1.2 names which group as part of the network kept communicating for Post-Construction Services?
o: Land title registries and notaries public
Foreign consular offices
Building research groups and utility providers
Homeowners' association election committees
n: Sec. 1.2 lists building owners, operators, architects, engineers, builders, manufacturers, building research groups, utility providers, furniture and equipment vendors, and building administrators/property managers. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.2)

q: For which category of buildings, facilities, or complexes does Sec. 1.3 allow an Architect to act as Building Administrator and/or Property Manager?
o: Government, religious, industrial, or recreational
Commercial, industrial, residential, or institutional
Commercial, agricultural, marine, or educational
Residential, industrial, heritage, or coastal
n: Sec. 1.3 refers to "a commercial, industrial, residential or institutional building, facility or complex." (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 1.3)

q: When it comes to evaluating how functionally effective the design and construction process was, Sec. 2.2.1(c) defines the Architect's role as what?
o: Independently overriding the original structural engineer's findings without consultation
Personally rebuilding any defective portions of the building
Revoking the building's occupancy permit
Helping the proper third parties evaluate the process's functional effectiveness
n: Sec. 2.2.1(c) frames the Architect's role as assisting the proper third parties in this evaluation, not acting unilaterally. (Source: SPP Document 205, Sec. 2.2.1(c))
